title: Weekly status report, assembled
sub: Three sources, every figure computed in code, one call for the sentences, and two checks over the draft before a person sends it.

nodes.l: Compute every figure the report may quote
One call writes the sentences between them
Check the draft in both directions
The week's report, with its failures named
A person reads it and sends it

steps.h: The timer fires: nothing decided anything
steps.d:
The same day every week, whatever kind of week it was.
The window runs from the last report, 09/11/2026,
to this one, 09/18/2026

The tracker export and the inbox are current to 09/18/2026
The time spreadsheet says it is current only to 09/15/2026,
which is reported rather than read as a week with no hours

steps.h: Your code reconciles the project names
steps.d:
Three systems spell the same project three ways
One name in the inbox matches nothing on the list and is
reported, not attached to the nearest project
steps.m: no model call: a table a person wrote once

steps.d:
38 figures: closed, opened, open, overdue, earliest due date,
hours against budget, threads waiting on us
4 are marked must say and are long enough to check
steps.m: no model call: this is the level-0 half

steps.h: One call, with the figures and the week's note
steps.d:
The model is handed every figure formatted exactly as it may
quote it, and writes the prose between them
It has nothing to look up and nothing to decide

steps.h: Your code checks the draft both ways
steps.d:
Every number in the draft has to be one of the figures
Every must-say figure has to appear in the draft
A draft that fails either is handed back, never patched

steps.h: A person reads it before it goes out
steps.d:
The checks cannot tell whether a real figure is sitting next
to the claim it belongs to, and the four must-say figures too
short to test are named for the reader to confirm by eye
steps.m: read before anyone acts on it
